changes.after: Command-line arguments are words passed to a program when it starts.

before: std::env::args yields Unicode command-line argument Strings. skip(1) omits the conventional program-name entry, then collect::<Vec<String>> stores the user arguments. args can panic on invalid Unicode. The args_os alternative for operating-system strings is an explicitly deferred platform-boundary reference; this worked invocation and its quiz use Unicode arguments only.

Run this example as ./app read for the worked output. A slice pattern [topic] matches exactly one argument, borrowing that String. The fallback handles zero or several user arguments without indexing a missing item. This is an application policy, not shell parsing implemented by Rust.

args.as_slice() borrows all elements of the argument vector as a slice. It neither consumes the vector nor copies its Strings; the slice pattern can inspect the borrowed length and entries.
Expected output or behavior: topic=read. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Pass a quoted two-word topic and explain how shell grouping differs from the Rust argument slice. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Command-line arguments are words passed to a program when it starts.
The program skips its own name. It prints a topic if exactly one word remains, or directions otherwise.
